headline: UPDATE to totw-20261025-0200-04 (Saturday Erbil drone strike) -- Iranian-side attribution + damage detail
dek: Mehr: 'As part of a drone operation carried out by the Revolutionary Guards' ground forces, the headquarters of the terrorist and separatist group Komala, located in the Balisan region, was targeted last night.' Komala: an explosive-laden Shahed drone struck its base in the Alana Valley, Balisan…
sources: Mehr News Agency via AFP (carried Gulf Today / Arab News); Komala statement via Arab Times Online
fault_line: Is Baghdad able -- or willing -- to stop Iranian strikes on Kurdish opposition camps on Iraqi soil, or is Iraq's Kurdistan now an open second front in the Iran war?

sections.what_happened: Mehr: 'As part of a drone operation carried out by the Revolutionary Guards' ground forces, the headquarters of the terrorist and separatist group Komala, located in the Balisan region, was targeted last night.' Komala: an explosive-laden Shahed drone struck its base in the Alana Valley, Balisan (~90 km NE of Erbil) at ~22:00 Saturday, causing damage to buildings/facilities with fighters safe and no casualties. No direct IRGC claim of responsibility has been published. Context: a similar Balisan strike hit Komala on Oct 17 (2 drones, material damage, no casualties per Rudaw); the deadliest recent strike killed 9 Komala members near Sulaymaniyah on July 17.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family counts: AFP T1 (Gulf Today credits AFP; Arab News carries the same AFP wire). Mehr has NO declared tier in the source registry, so it is reported with attribution but NEVER counts toward corroboration. Komala's statement is the subject's own claim, not independent corroboration. Reuters T1 already established the strike itself at 0200-04.
sections.what_disputed: The IRGC has not directly claimed the strike; attribution rests on Mehr (Iranian semi-official, unregistered tier) plus Komala's blame. Reuters' original item attributed the strike only to security sources, attacker unnamed. Komala's 'no casualties' claim is self-reported and unconfirmed by any third party.
sections.why_matters: While the world watches the Gulf, Tehran's war against its Kurdish opponents moves into the open -- its own media now naming the IRGC operation.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261025-0200-04 (Saturday Erbil drone strike) -- Iranian-side attribution + damage detail: Mehr reports an IRGC ground-forces drone operation hit Komala HQ in Balisan; Komala says a Shahed drone hit ~22:00 Saturday, material damage, no casualties

totw_analysis: Our read: While the world watches the Gulf, Tehran's war against its Kurdish opponents moves into the open -- its own media now naming the IRGC operation. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Baghdad able -- or willing -- to stop Iranian strikes on Kurdish opposition camps on Iraqi soil, or is Iraq's Kurdistan now an open second front in the Iran war?
